published_fields.description:
Cynthia Sheppard is a Seattle-area artist, art educator, and former MtG art director with over 15 years of history working with Wizards of the Coast.

Throughout her career, she's created character-driven illustration art for fantasy fiction and games like Magic: the Gathering and Dungeons & Dragons. Between 2015-2021, Cynthia served as a Sr. Art Director for Magic, leading the worldbuilding and art direction for sets such as Ixalan, Throne of Eldraine, Kaldheim, and Modern Horizons I & II. Since 2021, she's returned to illustrating full-time, and began mentoring art students on the side through SmarterArtSchool, many who now work as illustrators for Wizards of the Coast themselves.
An original MTG artist still creating images for the game.

Serena Malyon is a Canadian illustrator who works in watercolour, acryla gouache and Photoshop. She grew up in a household of artists and spent her early days drawing the knights and maidens from her books. Her illustrations blend whimsical stylization with contemporary compositions and colours to create a unique look. Her work has appeared in a variety of media, from young adult and fantasy book covers and interior illustrations to magazines, maps, picture books, textbooks, graphic novels, tabletop games and video games. She has been working for Magic: The Gathering since 2021.
Aaron Miller is an award-winning, world-renowned fantasy artist and illustrator whose richly painted illustrations have graced such brands as Magic: The Gathering, Star Wars, and Dungeons & Dragons.

Alayna Danner is a Magic artist who specializes in land images (and things made of crystal apparently!).  
Here is her cards:
https://scryfall.com/search?q=a%3A%E2%80%9Calayna+danner%E2%80%9D&unique=art&as=grid&order=name
Fine art oil painter and raptor educator

Alix Branwyn is an illustrator and designer living in the Seattle area. A varied work history as a former tattoo artist, poster artist, and UI artist for video games formed a foundation for her work on Magic: the Gathering and Dungeons and Dragons creating a wide span of imagery - from card art illustrations in both digital and traditional mediums to working on the concept side of things creating card frames for Booster Fun and faction motifs from the knotwork of Kaldheim to the New Capenna crime family symbols. Her most notable cards to date are The Eternal Wanderer, Amalia Benavides Aguirre, The Dragon-Kami Reborn, Battle at the Helvault with the accompanying Avacyn Token, Innkeeper’s Talent, and Teval’s Judgment.
Nino Vecia is a freelance illustrator working for companies and IP’s like Wizards Of The Coast, Magic the Gathering, Dungeons and Dragons, Blizzard, Marvel, and many more.

Bruce Brenneise (pronounced Bren-EYE-zee) is an award- winning illustrator. He is known for MTG cards such as Ancient Tomb, Godless Shrine, Bloodstained Mire, and Sword of Feast and Famine. He's also known for his work on other games like Dungeons and Dragons, Slay the Spire, and the Cosmere RPG. 

You can check out the full list of MTG cards here: https://scryfall.com/search?q=a%3A%E2%80%9CBruce+Brenneise%E2%80%9D&unique=art

Chase Stone is a New York based artist who has been creating artwork for Magic: The Gathering since 2011, with over 120 unique Magic card illustrations to his name.  His work for Wizards of the Coast also extends to Dungeons and Dragons, with numerous covers, interior illustrations and key art.  

Atlanta will be his first MagicCon!

Chris Rahn has been making art for Magic: the Gathering since 2007. Of the hundreds of cards he's illustrated, he is most well known for Craterhoof Behemoth, Cyclonic Rift, Sheoldred, the Apocalypse. He lives in the Seattle area and is married to fellow MtG artist, Alix Branwyn.

Chris has been a freelance illustrator in hobby games for over 26 years.  He is a graduate of the Columbus College of Art and Design where he earned his Bachelor of Fine Arts degree in Illustration.  His work can be seen in such properties as Dungeons & Dragons and Magic: The Gathering.  He has exhibited his art work around the world and is a award winning fantasy illustrator. Chris was also featured in the documentary Eye of the Beholder: the Art of Dungeons and Dragons (Amazon)

Danny Schwartz is a fantasy illustrator living in Westfield, New Jersey who specializes in whimsical, colorful acrylic paintings. His work has appeared in newspapers, magazines, books, games, television shows and galleries across the United States since he graduated from Syracuse in 2010. After all that, though, he decided to go back to the beginning -- aka spending hours and hours looking at and loving art on Magic Cards, and he has been happily illustrating regularly for Magic since 2022. He has over 30 cards in print with many more on the horizon.

His favorite card he's ever made is Bloom Tender from Lorwyn: Eclipsed, but he acknowledges that frogs a la Into the Flood Maw are a central part of his personal brand. He has never met a warm to cool color gradient he didn't like.

Daren Bader is an American fantasy illustrator, concept artist, and art director who has worked in the video game and tabletop gaming industries for over three decades. He is particularly recognized among card game players for his extensive contributions to Magic: The Gathering, having illustrated over 200 cards for the franchise using traditional oil and acrylic painting techniques.

His iconic MTG portfolio spans competitive staples, legendary creatures, and fan-favorite engine pieces across multiple eras, such as:
- Iconic Monsters & Legends: Akroma, Angel of Fury, Nadu, Winged Wisdom, Eight-and-a-Half-Tails, Jareth, Leonine Titan, Karn, Legacy Reforged, and Mirri, Cat Warrior.
- Powerful & Famous Enchantments: Oath of Druids, Hunting Grounds, Argothian Enchantress, Day of Destiny, Legacy's Allure, and Hidden Ancients.
- Famous Spells & Staples: Finale of Devastation, Gamble, Deep Analysis, Call to the Grave, Faceless Butcher, Condemn, and the widely reprinted Whispersilk Cloak.

Beyond his trading card legacy, Bader built a 20-year career as a Senior Art Director at Rockstar Games, spearheading the rugged visual identity for the ground-breaking Red Dead Redemption series, from Red Dead Revolver through Red Dead Redemption II. Following his work at Rockstar, he transitioned to spatial computing at Magic Leap and later served as the Studio Art Director for Secret Door Games, where he led visual development for the critically acclaimed tactical role-playing game Sunderfolk.

Bader has since returned to working as a full-time freelance illustrator. Outside of industry studio work, he is the artist behind Tribes of Kai, a fully painted 60-page graphic novel published by Flesk Publications that showcases his love for creature design and worldbuilding. His fantasy artwork has been selected for 15 editions of the prestigious Spectrum Fantastic Art annuals, and he was recently honored to have an illustration acquired by the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art for their permanent collection. He currently lives and works in Southern California.

David Palumbo is a traditional media artist who has been painting for Magic since 2008 with the release of Shards of Alara.  In the years since then, he's painted over 130 cards including the creation of Fblthp for the original Totally Lost.  

In addition to his work with Magic, Palumbo is known for moody genre illustrations and has done artwork for nearly two dozen illustrated novels and painted the entire 2020 Marvel Masterpieces trading card set.

The doodles that Douglas Shuler did across his schoolwork grew into an art career that spans almost 40 years, most notably as one of the original 25 Magic: The Gathering artists in the early 90's. He is known internationally for iconic art pieces including Serra Angel, Demonic Tutor, and Force of Nature. Since that time he has done nearly 150 cards across 20 expansions and has enjoyed developing his art style through experience with drawing, painting, digital art, video game concept illustrations and portraiture. As a jack-of-all-trades when it comes to creating an image, Douglas is equally comfortable using pencils, acrylics, airbrush, oil paints and digital mediums. Some of his work can be seen within numerous game and media companies including TSR, Wizards of the Coast, Lucasfilm, Paramount Pictures and the Sci-Fi Channel.

Eli Minaya is an illustrator and fine artist based in Virginia, USA. His early creative pursuits
began as a graffiti artist, which over time transformed into a varied career as an illustrator in
publishing; with clients such as Tor Books and Amazon Publishing, as well as Fantasy art with
clients such as Wizards of the Coast and Image Comics.
In his studio, he pushes the boundaries of collage art in pursuit of pure expression of the human
form, symbolism, and personal narrative.

Eric Deschamps is a Magic the Gathering card illustrator, as well as a children’s book illustrator. Eric's first Magic card was Goblin S.W.A.T. Team from the Unhinged set almost 20 years ago. Since then he's illustrated prominent planeswalker cards and Commander favorites, including Balefire Dragon; Celestial Colonnade; Chandra, Fire of Kaladesh; Dack Fayden; Elspeth, Sun's Champion; Esper Sentinel; Fatal Push; Giada, Font of Hope; Gideon, Ally of Zendikar; Nahiri, the Lithomancer; Olivia Voldaren; Ral Zarek; Tireless Tracker; and Tamiyo, the Moon Sage.

Gabor Szikszai is an illustrator and art director. He has been working in the Magic universe since 2005 (having illustrated nearly 200 cards), initially as the artistic partner of illustrator Zoltan Boros (Boros-Szikszai), and then under his own name starting in 2010. Between 2011 and 2025, he was primarily active in the gaming industry, serving as art director on titles such as Call of Duty, Skylanders, and Spellslingers, while putting his illustration work on the back burner (though he never stopped entirely); however, this year he has made it a priority again. His participation in this event is a tribute to the past 20 years, as well as a great momentum for his current new beginning.

Izzy is a larval kaiju with way too many stories to tell. Come visit a cosmic horror with a high charisma stat.

Click the store URL there to see what cards he’s sprinkled his evil magicks upon.

Signatures, commission orders, APs, Tokens, and Playmats will be available at the show!

If you can’t make it, or won’t be in Atlanta; Izzy’s Card Manager LEAH BENTLEY  is available to take your orders!
bentley.artmgmt@gmail.com

Jarel Threat is an award winning Fantasy and Comic Book Illustrator living in Rosenberg, Texas.
A graduate of Ringling College of Art and Design, Jarel works with oil paint, seeking to capture
beauty and strength with the use of subtle color and light. His work has been featured multiple
times in the Infected by Art annuals as well as the main show for Illuxcon.
Primarily known for his work for Magic: The Gathering, Jarel has had over 40 cards released
since starting in 2020. Over his 12 year career, he has also worked in books covers, card art,
album covers and comics. Other clients include Iron Crown Enterprises, Hit Point Press, 247
Comics, Verse Comics, Wraithmarked Creative, The Broken Binding, Straight Back Games and
a list of private art collectors.

Jeff Miracola has been a fantasy art pro since 1993 and has illustrated for properties such as Dungeons & Dragons, World of Warcraft, Mars Attacks, Star Wars, Planescape, Earthdawn, Shadowrun, and Magic: The Gathering, for which he's created more than 145 paintings.

Joe has been creating fantasy and sci-fi illustrations for roleplaying games, card games and books for three decades.  He began working on Magic the Gathering in 2016 with Hour of Devastation and has created over 70 cards total with the release of Secrets of Strixhaven. His most well known cards are Underworld Cookbook and Embercleave but has a number of cards that have seen play. Initially Joe worked digitally using Paintstorm Studio but began to switch to traditional painting methods with the  Kaldheim set in 2020 and today works exclusively traditional.

His other clients include; Beadle and Grimm's, Hit Point Press, Monte Cook Games, MCDM, Kobold Press, Ten Speed Press (Game of Thrones).

Josu Solano is an Illustrator and concept designer who has worked on Magic The Gathering since 2020, when he started on the Warhammer 40k UB set. From there he has worked on plenty of both Core and Universe Beyond sets as well as doing design work for some of those sets, including Secrets of Strixhaven and Reality Fracture. He is also working on DnD currently with WotC as well as upcoming MTG sets. His work is full of detail and a has a certain realism that he brings from working on feature films as well.

Justine Jones is a self taught artist and illustrator living in Philadelphia, known for her detailed linework and psychedelic colors.  She's done many cards for Magic the Gathering, most recently in Tarkir Dragonstorm!  Other notable appearances include: the Kaleidoscope Killers Secret Lair, Lotr poster cards, many dnd rulebook cards, and the Selfless Spirit promo.  You may have also seen her work on the cover of the new Dungeons and Dragons adventure anthology Dragon Delves, or the Ennie Award winning tabletop adventure, Halls of the Blood King.  Justine's work is heavily inspired by the comic books and video games that she grew up with, as well as fairy tales and mythology.

Kai Carpenter's paintings celebrate lush fantasy worlds and the wondrous beings who populate them. Through his work, he strives to impart the sense that you, too, inhabit these parts unknown. Kai's art has been featured in several publications including Spectrum, Infected by Art, Concept Art World and Juxtapose, and has appeared on trading cards, tabletop games, comic covers and in galleries as well as the national parks.

Hieu is an Australian artist from Melbourne who goes by the alias kelogsloops. His watercolour paintings often depict female portraiture inspired from surreal and fantasy art styles. Since beginning on his artistic career, he has worked and operated by his motto, “be right back, chasing dreams.” 
Hieu exhibits in galleries and shares his work with a growing community on social media. He first brought his art to Magic: The Gathering as a guest artist for a Secret Lair drop in June 2022, and has since continued collaborating with Wizards of the Coast on a number of new pieces.

With a career in games and publishing spanning over 25 years - Kieran has worked as an illustrator, concept artist and art director for such clients as Wizards of the Coast, Valve, Microsoft, Marvel, DC, Disney, Warner Bros, Penguin Random House and Baen. Born and raised in the Australian coastal city of Darwin, Kieran relocated to the United States of America at the age of 20 to pursue his dreams as a games and publishing artist. He currently works as a full time freelance artist for a variety of clientele at his studio in Tacoma.

Leon has been involved in the development of sets such as The brothers war, Phyrexia All Will Be One, Outlaws of Thunder Junction, Bloomburrow, Duskmourne, Aetherdrift and the recently released Tarkir: Dragonstorm.

As a card artist he typically works on cards that feature sprawling cityscapes, vibrant landscapes and huge machines. Such as: Cityscape leveler, the Clue edition Hallowed fountain and Stomping ground. The bloomburrow card Fountainport and more recently a basic land cycle featuring Avishkar in Aetherdrift, and a Sol ring for Tarkir: Dragonstorm. When not working on various MTG projects, Leon can be found building Lego kits, pretending to be an athlete on the athletics track or spending time with his cats Mimi and Momo.

Lucas Graciano is an award winning artist whose professional work spans back to 2004. He has worked on Magic since 2009 with 200+ illustrated cards.  Some of his more notable cards include: Thoughtseize (Theros), Murktide Regent, Simian Spirit Guide, Phlage, Titan of Fire’s Fury, Vampiric Tutor, and Up the Beanstalk.  His most recent MtG work includes Eridu, Carrier of Dawn and Quandrix the Proof.

Mark was born in Sitka, Alaska, a sublime but wet locale under the North Star. When younger, Mark wanted to be an astronaut. As a result, he started drawing pictures of outer space and flying saucers-soon including monsters and creatures in the illustrations. His appetite to draw grew as the years went by, but it wasn't until Mark was in Junior High School that he decided to pursue a career in art. 

After high school, Mark went to college at Gonzaga University in Spokane, Washington, to expand and hone his artistic talents. While there he took many classes outside of art because they provided information about a variety of subjects and helped Mark come up with ideas. In particular, he liked science courses. Following Gonzaga, Mark went on to receive his master's degree in fine arts at Washington University in St. Louis, Missouri. He then packed his bags and joined his friend Anson to work in Seattle.

Mark's freelance work for Wizards of the Coast began shortly after he arrived in the Emerald City. For him it was, and still is, a dream come true: drawing strange creatures and environments and making a living at it!

From 1997 - 2000, Mark also worked on site at Wizards of the Coast as a staff conceptual artist. Until 2016, he'd also been teaching illustration, visual composition, and figure drawing part-time at the Northwest College of Art and Design.

Mark has been freelancing illustrative and conceptual design work for thirty-four years and has loved every minute of it.

Hi, I`m Mathias Kollros, artist from Austria and best known for my Sci-Fi and Fantasy illustrations.
My work ranges from scary to whimsical and has a heavy focus on story telling, characters and creature design.
Since 2011 I have the pleasure to help bring fantastical creatures and mythical monsters to life within Magic the Gathering.
If you are interested in signatures, sketches or alterations visit me at my booth. Looking forward to see everyone there!

Mike Bierek is a professional illustrator and concept artist renowned for his contributions to Magic: The Gathering, with over 100 cards featuring his artwork, including iconic pieces like Stoneforge Mystic, Drana, Liberator of Malakir, and illustrations for sets such as Zendikar, Innistrad: Midnight Hunt, and others. 
After breaking into the industry in 2008 with Massive Black Inc., he freelanced for major game studios including Ubisoft, Bethesda, and Riot Games, producing concept art and illustrations for prominent titles. He also maintains an active career as a tattoo artist at Legion Art Collective in the Sacramento, California area, where he applies his dynamic fantasy style to custom work. 
Bierek continues to create original Magic art, artist proofs, and hand-painted card alters while balancing his tattoo business.

Paul is a Scottish art director, illustrator and game designer with over 17 years of experience working in the games industry.
His credits include Magic: the Gathering, Dungeons & Dragons, Warhammer, Silent Hill: Townfall, Daggerheart, Guild Wars 2 and Destiny 2.
He is currently developing his own game, the horror TTRPG, Pale Tides and he WIILL talk about it. He will also draw furbies on all of your cards, sorry.

Phil Stone was given up by the wolves and raised by his parents.  He was born in the 70’s, raised in the 80’s, went into hiding in the 90’s, and is still trying to figure out the 2000’s.  Phil Stone was a self taught artist until as of late, he decided to pursue his degree in illustration.  Don’t let the diploma fool you, his art is fueled by coffee, cigarettes,  and night terrors.  Over the years, Phil Stone has had the opportunity to work with some wonderful people, some are listed below, some would rather not be mentioned.

Wizards of the Coast  - Magic:  the Gathering, Dungeons and Dragons -GLOOMHAVEN -  Beadle & Grimm - Heavy Play, GREYHAWK, Blackmoor, DeathBringer -Luke Gygax/ Gaxx Worx - SHADOWDARK,  Legendary Games - Bloat Games - Pelgrane Press - Kobold Press - Dark Wizard Games - Enworld.org - - “Some Guy Named Skeeter” - Frog God Games - Total Party Kill Games - Wizco Games  JUST TO NAME A FEW

Chris is an illustrator with over 20 years of experience. He started working for Magic the Gathering in 2014 and his first cards were published in 2015. Since then he's been working almost exclusively for Wizards of the Coast. He has created about 160 distinct cards, including some iconic Planewalkers like Teferi Hero of Dominaria, Liliana Dreadhorde General and Kaya Ghost Assassin. He's working digitally and traditionally.

From 1995's Ice Age to recent releases like Star Trek and Reality Fracture, Randy's 250+ illustrations for Magic have included many staples across multiple formats, including Lorien Revealed, Dance of the Dead, Soul Warden, Fierce Guardianship, and Requiting Hex.

He works primarily in traditional oil and acrylic paints, shifting to digital as required, moving easily between heroic figurative to lands, to artifacts or saga art, as needed.

Randy and his wife Monica look forward to meeting you at MagicCon: Atlanta. They are high school sweethearts, together since Randy was 15.

Richard Kane Ferguson is an internationally renowned fantasy artist, comic artist and illustrator who has worked extensively in the gaming industry since the 1990s. He's been painting and designing for MTG almost since its beginning, working on its earliest sets right up to the present day. He's lent his distinctive visual style to a host of iconic cards from Dakkon Blackblade to Force of Will. And he's probably at his creative happiest when chained to his drawing board and cranking on a really tight MTG deadline.
rk post has been a Magic: the Gathering artist for more than 28 years with more works appearing next year!  Come by, say hello, check out the shop (check out instantly), and/or get some cards singed!

Ryan Pancoast has illustrated over 200 cards for Magic. Working in oils, he has illustrated popular characters including Urza, Planeswalker, Etali, Primal Conqueror, and Isshin, Two Heavens as One. He has also illustrated longtime favorites such as Young Wolf, Unburied Rites, and Zuran Orb.

Sam Burley is a Seattle-based fantasy artist who’s worked on MTG since 2011, contributing concept art for dozens of sets and creating over 150 card illustrations. A love for towering mountains and billowing clouds has led his art to be primarily environment focused, but he is a fan of critters both inside and outside of illustration, too! His most popular cards include Pantlaza, Tayam, Supreme Verdict, Prismatic Vista, The Ozolith, and many basic lands including the full-art ‘Nyx’ cycle from Theros Beyond Death.

Sources allege there are other interesting things about him, these reports cannot be verified as he is highly reclusive and rarely seen in the wild. Please note that Sam is quite skittish, so approach with caution if spotted, and ideally, bring dogs to pet.

As an artist working predominantly in the gaming industry since the mid 90's, Steve Prescott has brought his lively illustrating style to numerous products from such companies as White Wolf Games, FASA, Paizo, Blizzard, Copenhagen Creators, Brotherwise Games, Animal Planet, Larian Studios, Draco Games, DHX Media, Valve, Bethesda, Hasbro, and most notably for Wizards of the Coast where he has contributed heavily to both Dungeons & Dragons and even more so to Magic:the Gathering as a multi-faceted concept designer, illustrator, and painter. Steve has illustrated close to 300 individual MtG cards and his conceptual design credits include Lorwyn, Innistrad, Ixalan, Theros, Kaldheim, Neon Dynasty, Brothers War, Thunder Junction, Dragonstorm, Bloomburrow, as well as upcoming sets.

Steven Belledin was raised in Pennsylvania and started his career completing highschool art assignments for his older sisters in exchange for enough money to buy more Swedish fish than he probably should have eaten. After high school he fled small town life to hide among the drones of New York City and become an oil painter. Four years later, he stumbled out of the gates of Brooklyn's Pratt Institute into the harsh light of the "real world" and immediately dove head first into the brick wall of illustration. Though it took him a couple years to recover, he finally began plying his trade in 2000 and continues to plod ahead, tickled that he gets paid to do something he loves. Steven currently resides in Ballston Spa, New York, peering out at the world through the slats of the venetian blinds in his studio windows.

An established fantasy illustrator, Kaja started doing work for Magic with "Antiquities", and appeared in most sets through-out the 90's, before turning her talents to co-writing the Hugo Award winning webcomic Girl Genius with her husband, Phil. This is still going strong. Recently, she has again done work for Wizards, appearing in the new "Hobbit" set.

Phil has been busy in the fields of science-fiction, comics, gaming, and steampunk since 1980. He started working for Magic with "Ice Age" and was in most sets through the halcyon 90's. With the new century, he began work on Girl Genius, the Hugo Award winning webcomic he creates with his wife, Kaja. Recently, he has been asked to create new cards for Wizards of the Coast, and had a Secret Lair come out last year.

Svetlin Velinov is a globally acclaimed Bulgarian artist whose work has become a cornerstone of the entertainment and gaming industries. Specializing in illustration, concept art, and comics, Velinov’s distinct style is recognized by fans of high-fantasy art worldwide. Born in Varna, Velinov demonstrated a profound interest in the arts from an early age. He laid his creative foundation at the Dobri Hristov National School of Arts in Varna before moving to Sofia to study Animation Direction at the New Bulgarian University. Velinov began his professional career in 2002 as a graphic designer and freelance artist. However, his most significant career milestone began 16 years ago when he joined the core illustration team at Wizards of the Coast.

His contributions have been vital to the visual identity of Magic: The Gathering, the world’s premier trading card game. His achievements include:
- Prolific Output: With over 400 illustrations created for the franchise, he is currently the second most prolific artist in the history of the game since its inception in 1993.
- Artistic Influence: His work spans iconic creatures, powerful spells, and immersive landscapes that have defined the look of various MTG "planes" for over a decade.

Baxa has been a pro illustrator for over 35 years, for high profile clients. His visceral, innovative character designs and story infused illustrations have been featured in books, magazines, collectible card games (MTG), rpgs (D&D)miniatures, video games, special fx make-up, film and more. As of late, he is expanding his personal work and IPs for publishing and exhibition in galleries in Los Angeles, where he is a member of the LA Dark Art Society movement. Baxa is a published author of Get Work as a Fantasy Artist, and Blood Rituals: The Art of Tom Baxa, and is currently writing and painting an illustrated horror novel, Zombie Coven, featured in his Patreon www.patreon.com/BaxaArt. He enjoys exploring dark themes of the human condition, in order to better understand what drives people. His artwork, prints, books, and more can be seen at www.BaxaArt.com.

yler Jacobson is an award-winning illustrator of fantasy and science fiction. His extensive body of work includes countless pieces for Magic: The Gathering and Dungeons & Dragons. Additionally, Jacobson’s illustrations have appeared in multiple books and magazines with Simon & Schuster, TOR, Entertainment Weekly, Rolling Stone, Men’s Journal, Runner's World, Texas Monthly, The Weekly Standard, and Scientific American, among others. He’s been the recipient of both the Jack Gaughan award (2010) and the Spectrum Gold award (2012). He graduated from the Academy of Art University in San Francisco in 2009 with an MFA in illustration. In partnership with Flesk Publicatons, Tyler recently published his first art book, "The Art of Tyler Jacobson."

Tyler Walpole is a celebrated Magic artist that has been working on the game since 2017. In addition to painting fan-favorites like Hakbal of the Surging Soul and Ur-Dragon, he's also been flagged as an artist that specializes in a 2D animation-inspired style. Because of this, he's produced art for several animation related Secret Lairs, including: Spongebob Internet Sensation, Saturday Morning D&D, and the Real Ghostbusters!

Tom Wanerstrand is an American illustrator and Print Production professional in the games industry. The son of Swedish immigrants, Tom began his game career by becoming one of the original 25 illustrators for the seminal game Magic: The Gathering in 1993. He then began a 30-year long journey in the production trade for the game's publisher, Wizards of the Coast. Along the way, Tom continued to illustrate over 60 different unique cards for Magic: The Gathering. His most well known works include classics such as Royal Assassin from the original Alpha release, and Blood Moon from MTG: The Dark. An avid snow skier and boater, you can often find Tom in the mountains and waterways of the beautiful Pacific Northwest region of the U.S. where he lives on an island in the Salish Sea with his wife, son and two occasionally-well-behaved dogs.

A fifteen year veteran artist of Magic the Gathering, Vincent has provided art for many popular and iconic cards. Cards such as Ulamog the Defiler, Emrakul the Eons Torn, Polluted Delta, the Zendikar full art lands, Rakdos Lord of Riots, Day of Judgment, Kroxa Titan of Death's Hunger, Uro Titan of Nature's Wrath, and more. When Vincent isn't busy doing Magic card art, he works as a concept artist & creature designer for such horror films as IT Chapter Two, Scary Stories to Tell in the Dark, and Smile and Smile 2.

Winona Nelson has been creating art for Magic: the Gathering since 2009, with her first cards released in Innistrad.  Her best known cards are "Tymna the Weaver," "Azusa, Lost But Seeking," and "Flash Photography." This will be her first Magicon!

Hi! I'm Josiah "Jo" Cameron, I've been illustrating for Magic the Gathering and D&D since 2023, and playing since 2015.

I first started playing Magic 11 years ago. The game reignited my interest in Scifi/Fantasy illustration and years later, thanks to the help of mentors and friends, here I am. 
I love playing and illustrating for this game. I mostly play EDH in Jund colors, Dragons and Lands. 

Some of my notable cards and tokens are: Dack Fayden, Helping Hand(FRC), Entropic Battlecruiser (EOE), Start Your Engines/Max Speed Token(DFT), Sylvan Scavenging (FDN), Quakestrider Ceratops (FDN),  Steelburr Champion and Offspring (BLC), Gluttonous Hellkite (MH3), Generous Plunderer Showcase (BIG).

Born in 1996, Ben did not start pursuing
art seriously until he was eighteen.
Without any sort of local schools or
classes, he chose to be a self-taught
digital and traditional artist. Over the
last 8 years Ben spent most of his focus
taking mentorships under artists such as
Scott M Fischer, Winona Nelson, David
Palumbo and Cynthia Sheppard with a
focus on Magic: The Gathering Art In his
work. His work has been published in
Spectrum and Infected By Art. He has a
love for experimenting with movement,
texture, and pattern and tries to learn
something new with every piece.

Hey There! I'm Andrew, or more specifically, "SchmandrewART." I'm an award-winning illustrator whose work is bright, energetic, and full of emotion. Although my artistic roots began in the world of screen printing and contemporary pop art, my subject matter shifted into what I like to call "fantasy pop."

Since 2013, I've created work for notable clients, including BioWare, SuperMassive Games, Boom!, Lucasfilm, Bethesda Games, Mondo, Sony, Variety Magazine, BoJack Horseman, Reebok, Marvel, and Wizards of the Coast. In that time, I've shown my work at Gallery1988, Gallery Nucleus, The GenCon Art Show, Spectrum: Fantastic Art, Dragon Con, and many other conventions across the country. In addition to that, I'm also continually developing my own body of personal work while traveling across the country for conventions!

published_fields.bio: An original 1993 MTG artist still working with the wonderful team at Wizards of the Coast.

Cynthia Sheppard is a Seattle-area artist, art educator, and former MtG art director with over 15 years of history working with Wizards of the Coast.

Throughout her career, she's created character-driven illustration art for fantasy fiction and games like Magic: the Gathering and Dungeons & Dragons. Between 2015-2021, Cynthia served as a Sr. Art Director for Magic, leading the worldbuilding and art direction for sets such as Ixalan, Throne of Eldraine, Kaldheim, and Modern Horizons I & II. Since 2021, she's returned to illustrating full-time and enjoys meeting fans of Magic at events.

Serena Malyon is a Canadian illustrator who works in watercolour, acryla gouache and Photoshop. She grew up in a household of artists and spent her early days drawing the knights and maidens from her books. Her illustrations blend whimsical stylization with contemporary compositions and colours to create a unique look. Her work has appeared in a variety of media, from young adult and fantasy book covers and interior illustrations to magazines, maps, picture books, textbooks, graphic novels, tabletop games and video games.
She has been working for Magic: The Gathering since 2021.

Aaron Miller is an award-winning, world-renowned fantasy artist and illustrator whose richly painted illustrations have graced such brands as Magic: the Gathering, Star Wars, and Dungeons & Dragons. Companies that feature Aaron's work include Hasbro/Wizards of the Coast, Blizzard Entertainment, EBAY, Hit Point Press, Fantasy Flight Games, Sony Online Entertainment, Mercury Retrograde Press, Catalyst Games, Posthuman Studios, and Alderac Entertainment Group, among others.

Miller's oil and digital work has earned numerous accolades and awards. His art was included multiple times in the fantasy art field's prestigious publication, Spectrum: The Best in Fantastic Art. lllustration West 57 2018 has awarded a Gold Award for Graphic Novels/Comic Books. Miller was MileHiCon's 2013 Artist Guest of Honor and Best Color Award Winner. GenCon, the world's biggest gaming convention, bestowed him with honors two years running: 2013 Best in Show and 2010 Juror's Choice Award.

Miller's art has been displayed at galleries across the United States. Notably, his work hung in the Mazza Museum in Findlay, Ohio, as part of its annual Enchanted Brush Exhibit and has been featured in J. Anthony Kosar's Maleficium Dark Art Exhibit in Chicago. Miller was also honored with a solo exhibit of his masterful paintings at the Illinois State Museum in July 2015.

Passionate about painting, especially capturing the human form, Miller looks to great painters and illustrators of the past for inspiration, which is evident by the rich brushstrokes and dynamic forms he brings to life on canvas. In the tradition of great master painters and advocacy for the advancement of other artists, Miller is an instructor for the Fantasy Art Workshop held during the summer in Milwaukee, WI.

Alayna Danner is a fantasy illustrator from Seattle, Washington. She specializes in painting landscapes and cityscapes. Her work is primarily in Photoshop and occasionally works in acrylic and watercolor.  When she isn't drawing, she's likely walking her dog Hank, hanging with her cats, or playing a variety of games: JRPGs, D&D, Magic, or board games.  She grew up in Madison, Wisconsin drawing anime and video game characters.   After playing Magic: The Gathering in high school she decided that was what she wanted to pursue- a career illustrating Magic cards.  She attended the Milwaukee Institute of Art and Design, which gave her a good background in art and she learned tips from Magic illustrator & MIAD teacher John Matson on how to work towards a career doing fantasy art. Alayna fulfilled her dream to illustrate for Magic: The Gathering in 2016 and hasn't stopped working for Wizards of the Coast since.  Her first card was Supreme Will from Hour of Devastation.  Since then, she's illustrated over 130 cards, including Jeweled Lotus, Otawara The Soaring City, Alpine Moon, Bloodforged Battle-Axe, a bunch of new art variants of Magic card classics such as Marsh Flats, Verdant Catacombs, Nykthos, Shrine to Nyx; Godless Shrine, Evolving Wilds, and a ton of basic (and non-basic) lands.  She is thrilled to be illustrating for Magic and continues to play Commander (her Commander decks are Linvala, Keeper of Silence & Jinnie Fay) and drafts as often as her schedule allows.  Her favorite Magic card that she illustrated is Animal Sanctuary, as her cats and dog are in the illustration.
Chase Stone has been creating concept art and illustrations for Magic for over ten years, with more than 100 cards to his name.  Atlanta will be his first MagicCon!

Chris Rahn has been making art for Magic: the Gathering since 2007. Of the hundreds of cards he's illustrated, he is most well known for Craterhoof Behemoth, Cyclonic Rift, Sheoldred, the Apocalypse. He lives in the Seattle area and is married to fellow MtG artist, Alix Branwyn.

I'm a self-taught professional artist. Most of my work is digital, but I
also use traditional media. I was born in 1976 and grew up in Athens,
Greece. As far back as I can remember, I've always had a pencil in my
hand, doodling all the time. As a kid, and later as a teenager, I drew
inspiration from books by J. Verne, R. E. Howard, E. A. Poe and H. P.
Lovecraft. My favourite artists were F. Frazzeta, L. Royo, P. E. Serpieri
and S. Toppi. In 1994 I applied to the Athens School of Fine Art, but I got
rejected. The same year I was hired as a junior artist for an animation
studio. My professional career as a freelance illustrator started in 1999.
Several years were spent working for various advertising agencies,
when I decided to put my mind, heart, and soul into what I always loved,
putting my own imagination on paper.
Since August 2012 I'm based in England, working as a fantasy
illustrator. In late 2013 I've started working almost exclusively for
Wizards of the Coast. My first cards were published in 2015 for Dragons
of Tarkir. Since then, I've been creating artwork for many cards and
packaging, as well as interior illustrations and book covers for Dungeons
& Dragons. Both games are so diverse and extensive; and every brief is
different. I love painting the human form in any of it's shapes and
postures, and I reckon that is obvious in my work.

Chris has been a freelance illustrator in hobby games for over 20 years.  He is a graduate of the Columbus College of Art and Design where he earned his Bachelor of Fine Arts degree in Illustration.  His work can be seen in such properties as Skylanders, Dungeons & Dragons, Kaijudo: Duel Masters, World of Warcraft, Harry Potter, Hearthstone, Pathfinder, Magic: The Gathering and is a contributor to Imagine FX Magazine and 3D Total magazine.   

 His personal and professional work has appeared in Spectrum 19, 20, 21 and 22, won the Silver Award in the Editorial category in 23, and 24 the best in contemporary science fiction and fantasy art from around the world.

Daren Bader is an acclaimed illustrator, art director, and concept artist widely recognized for his prolific work in the fantasy genre, gaming industry, and traditional oil painting field. Over his career, he has illustrated over 200 cards for Magic: the Gathering, starting with Tempest. Famous cards include Oath of Druids, Mirri, Cat Warrior, and Akroma, Angel of Fury, to just name a few. Additionally, he worked as a Senior Art Director and Concept Artist for Rockstar Games for 20 years, creating essential mood pieces, environmental studies, and cinematic concepts for the entire Red Dead Redemption franchise. He has also contributed to other legendary franchises including D&D, Warhammer and properties from Capcom and Blizzard.

David Palumbo has been working as a freelance illustrator in traditional media since 2006 and creating artwork for Magic: the Gathering since 2008.  His work is best known for combining painterly realism with moody and dynamic genre subjects and has featured on numerous book, comic, and magazine covers as well as comprising the entirety of the 2020 Marvel Masterpieces trading card set and creating the beloved character Fblthp for the 2013 MtG Gatecrash card Totally Lost.

The doodles that Douglas Shuler did across his schoolwork grew into an art career that spans almost 40 years, most notably as one of the original 25 Magic: The Gathering artists in the early 90's. He is known internationally for iconic art pieces including Serra Angel, Demonic Tutor, and Force of Nature. Since that time he has done nearly 150 cards across 20 expansions and has enjoyed developing his art style through experience with drawing, painting, digital art, video game concept illustrations and portraiture. As a jack-of-all-trades when it comes to creating an image, Douglas is equally comfortable using pencils, acrylics, airbrush, oil paints and digital mediums. Some of his work can be seen within numerous game and media companies including TSR, Wizards of the Coast, Lucasfilm, Paramount Pictures and the Sci-Fi Channel.

Eric Deschamps is a Magic the Gathering card illustrator, as well as a children's book illustrator. Eric's first Magic card was Goblin S.W.A.T. Team from the Unhinged set almost 20 years ago. Since then he's illustrated prominent planeswalker cards and Commander favorites, including Balefire Dragon; Celestial Colonnade; Chandra, Fire of Kaladesh; Dack Fayden; Elspeth, Sun's Champion; Esper Sentinel; Fatal Push; Giada, Font of Hope; Gideon, Ally of Zendikar; Nahiri, the Lithomancer; Olivia Voldaren; Ral Zarek; Tireless Tracker; and Tamiyo, the Moon Sage.

Gabor Szikszai is an illustrator and art director. He has been working in the Magic universe since 2005 (having illustrated nearly 200 cards), initially as the artistic partner of illustrator Zoltan Boros (Boros-Szikszai), and then under his own name starting in 2010. Between 2011 and 2025, he was primarily active in the gaming industry, serving as art director on titles such as Call of Duty, Skylanders, and Spellslingers, while putting his illustration work on the back burner (though he never stopped entirely); however, this year he has made it a priority again. His participation in this event is a tribute to the past 20 years, as well as a great momentum for his current new beginning.

Izzy is a veteran lead concept artist, illustrator, writer, and art director with a specialty in world building and narrative development. 

Magic: The Gathering (Animated Series), League of Legends, Call of Duty, God of War, Magic: The Gathering (TCCG), Dungeons & Dragons, are just some of the many projects on which Izzy has contributed or led.

After taking a break from the industry and spending several years developing original IPs and adventuring in Mexico aboard his sailboat, Izzy has settled back in his home country of the United States.

Now based in the Pacific Northwest, Izzy continues to be an avid traveler, writer, gamer, and reader, developing new stories, comics, and art.

Jason has been creating art for the publishing and entertainment markets for the past 24 years, and his career has spanned many fields of fantasy and genre art, including card games, miniatures, comics, concept art, fine art, and hundreds of covers to books, games, magazines, albums, and t-shirts. His contributions to the art of Magic has spanned much of that time, and is the work he is best known for today. It includes many notable cards, including 2 planeswalkers, 2 masterpieces, over 40 mythic rares, and he is perhaps best known for the constellation gods series, which comprises 35 cards including a secret lair set.

Jeff Miracola has been a professional illustrator since 1993 and has illustrated for properties such as Dungeons & Dragons, World of Warcraft, Mars Attacks, Star Wars, Earthdawn, Shadowrun, as well as Magic the Gathering, for which he has illustrated over 145 cards. Jeff's work also includes conceptual toy and video game design, advertising and editorial illustration, and children's books for clients such as Target, Electronic Arts, ImagineFX Magazine, Scholastic, and more.

Jeff's honors include a Gold Award in Infected by Art vol. 2, Silver Award from Spectrum: the Best in Fantastic Art, being 2011 GenCon Artist Guest of Honor, and having his work exhibited in multiple museum exhibits, such as Masters of Science Fiction & Fantasy Art (Kenosha Public Museum), Dream Worlds: The Art of Imaginative Realism (Canton Museum of Art), Enchanted Brush(Mazza Museum), and Worldbuilders (South Bend Museum of Art) alongside legendary artist Michael Whelan

With a career in games and publishing spanning over 20 years - Kieran has worked as an illustrator, concept artist, UI artist and art director for such clients as Wizards of the Coast, Microsoft, Marvel, Disney, Warner Bros and Sony Online Entertainment. 
Born and raised in the Australian coastal city of Darwin, Kieran relocated to the United States of America at the age of 20 to pursue his dreams as a games and publishing artist. He currently works as a full time freelance artist for a variety of clientele at his studio in Tacoma, Washington.

Lucas Graciano has been working on Magic the Gathering since 2009, with over 140 card illustrations in the game. Some of his more popular contributions include: Thoughtseize (Theros), Grave Titan (PROMO), and the more recently Murktide Regent, Simian Spirit Guide, and Bloodtithe Harvester.

You'll find more information about Lucas on his website: www.lucasgraciano.com

Growing up in the sublime locale of Sitka, Alaska, Mark had dreams of flying saucers and epic landscapes, rarely putting his pencil down as a result. After furthering his art studies at Gonzaga University and Washington University in St. Louis, he heard the call from a friend to do some work for Wizards of the Coast, drawing and painting an endless array of fanciful creatures & characters, both as a freelance illustrator and staff concept artist. These past thirty years it was, and still is for him a dream come true: drawing strange creatures and environments and making a living at it.

The Austrian artist Mathias Kollros is known for his Scifi and Fantasy illustrations.
His work ranges from scary to whimsical and has a heavy focus on story telling, characters and creature design.
For over a decade his paintings bring fantastical creatures and mythical monsters to life.

schedules.title: Draw with a Magic Artist: Mathias Kollros
schedules.description: Come learn to draw from one of the artists who helps bring Magic to life!  They'll take you through a step-by-step lesson where you will walk away with your very own sketch that you created! This activity is geared to all ages, and no drawing experience is necessary.

published_fields.bio: Illustrator specializing in fantastic and science-fiction art.

Alix Branwyn is an illustrator and designer living in the Seattle area. A varied work history as a former tattoo artist, poster artist, and UI artist for video games formed a foundation for her work on Magic: the Gathering and Dungeons and Dragons creating a wide span of imagery - from card art illustrations in both digital and traditional mediums to working on the concept side of things creating card frames for Booster Fun and faction motifs such as the knotwork of Kaldheim and the New Capenna crime family symbols.

Eli Minaya is an illustrator and fine artist based in Virginia, USA. His early creative pursuits began as a graffiti artist, which over time transformed into a varied career as an illustrator in publishing; with clients such as Tor Books and Amazon Publishing, as well as Fantasy art with clients such as Wizards of the Coast and Image Comics. In his studio, he pushes the boundaries of collage art in pursuit of pure expression of the human form, symbolism, and personal narrative. He has taught numerous students that the core of any creative endeavor must be joy, as It drives his own work. Joy in creating, in forming ideas, in the search of an artist's personal voice. Eli's own voice sings loudly in the works of art he creates.

Evyn Fong is a Seattle-based concept artist and illustrator working for Magic the Gathering and Dungeons and Dragons.  She has produced both illustrations as well as worldbuilding concept art for Magic, including for Neon Dynasty Kamigawa and the new Eldraine.

Joe spent his early life in Kentucky before moving to Cincinnati to attend The Art Academy of Cincinnati. He eventually crossed paths with Richard Luschek who taught him more about traditional painting. He's stayed in the northern Kentucky/Cincinnati area ever since. Since college Joe has created artwork for video games, roleplaying games, card games, and books in a variety of styles. He loves a wide array of subjects in his art but tends to focus on light and texture. He has worked as an illustrator, sequential artist, colorist, concept artist, and art director for various companies throughout his career. All of his work is made using oils, acrylics or Paintstorm Studio.
https://www.girlgeniusonline.com/comic.php

Leon Tukker is a concept artist and Illustrator from the Netherlands. Since 2020 he has been involved with the worldbuilding team of WOTC  as a freelance concept artist to develop sets such as, The brothers war. Phyrexia all will be one. Outlaws of thunder junction, Bloomburrow, Duskmourne, Aetherdrift and the recently released Tarkir: Dragonstorm.

As a card artist he typically works on cards that feature sprawling cityscapes, vibrant landscapes and huge machines. Such as: Cityscape leveler, the Clue edition Hallowed fountain and Stomping ground. The bloomburrow card Fountainport and more recently a basic land cycle featuring Avishkar in Aetherdrift, and a Sol ring for Tarkir: Dragonstorm. When not working on various MTG projects, Leon can be found building Lego kits, pretending to be an athlete on the athletics track or spending time with his cats Mimi and Momo.

Mike Bierek is a professional illustrator and concept artist renowned for his contributions to Magic: The Gathering, with over 100 cards featuring his artwork, including iconic pieces like Stoneforge Mystic, Drana, Liberator of Malakir, and illustrations for sets such as Zendikar, Innistrad: Midnight Hunt, and others. After breaking into the industry in 2008 with Massive Black Inc., he freelanced for major game studios including Ubisoft, Bethesda, and Riot Games, producing concept art and illustrations for prominent titles. He also maintains an active career as a tattoo artist at Legion Art Collective in the Sacramento, California area, where he applies his dynamic fantasy style to custom work. He continues to create original Magic art, artist proofs, and hand-painted card alters while balancing his tattoo business.

I'm Alessandra, I'm an award winning illustrator and fine artist. I began creating fantasy art at a very young age as both an escape and refuge. The worlds and characters I created as a child have followed me throughout my journey as an artist as I continue to create similar subjects to this day. However instead of using colored pencils and markers to bring my visions to life I use oil paint now.

 ¹
Client lists include: Wizards of the Coast, Sideshow Collectibles, Fantasy Flight Games, Upper Deck, Catalyst Game Labs.

 ¹

Work published in Spectrum 24, 25, 26, and 27.

schedules.title: Birds of Prey with Magic Artist Alessandra Pisano
schedules.description: Experiance the beauty and mystique of owls up close! Meet a real Maha while learning about raptors, conservation and the history and importance of falconry. You'll leave this program with more bird facts then you'll know what to do with and a road map to get involved with raptors if you so choose! Take all the photos you want, this program is open to all ages.

published_fields.bio: Andrea Radeck is a MTG artist with about 30 cards, ranging from cute and cuddly to the howling wolf token from Innestrad. She can be seen on a number of Un-sets, did 5 years of Star City Games' Creature collection, and has been working on her comic for about 4 years.

published_fields.bio: Danny Schwartz is a fantasy illustrator and character designer living in Westfield, New Jersey. His work has appeared in newspapers, magazines, books, games, television shows and galleries across the United States for over a decade. Recent clients include: Wizards of the Coast (Magic: The Gathering), Wyrmwood Gaming, Viacom/CBS (Late Nite Cartoons), Orbit Books (The Witcher), and Thousand Ant/Unity Engine, among many others. His work has also appeared in Gallery Nucleus's LA and Portland, OR locations, and he is a regular contributor to both WOWxWOW and Every Day Original, both online galleries which sell original works of art for collectors all around the world.

Jarel Threat is an award winning Fantasy and Comic Book Illustrator living in Rosenberg, Texas.
A graduate of Ringling College of Art and Design, Jarel works with oil paint, seeking to capture
beauty and strength with the use of subtle color and light. His work has been featured multiple
times in the  Å“Infected by Art  annuals as well as the main show for Illuxcon.

Primarily known for his work for Magic: The Gathering, Jarel has had over 40 cards released
since starting in 2020. Over his 12 year career, he has also worked in books covers, card art,
album covers and comics. Other clients include Iron Crown Enterprises, Hit Point Press, 247
Comics, Verse Comics, Wraithmarked Creative, The Broken Binding, Straight Back Games and
a list of private art collectors.

Follow his art journey on his Instagram and Twitter: @jarelthreat
Portfolio: www.jarelthreat.com
Youtube: www.youtube.com/c/JarelThreat

Phil Stone was given up by the wolves and raised by his parents. He was born in the 70's, raised in the 80's, and became a failed comic book artist in the 90's. 
In the 2000's, Phil gave up the pen and became a "D List" celebrity hairdresser, travelling the world and performing on stage with the latest coifs, 
and styling hair for long forgotten celebs. It wasn't until several years ago that Phil got a second chance at illustration. 
Phil ran like a banshee in the night with this new opportunity to make it happen. He has graced the inner pages of such 
RPG's as Kobold Press, Planet X games, Enworld, and Palladium Books to name a few out of the many. 
His art can be seen in 8 cards for Forgotten Realms, 11 cards in Baulders Gate, 2 in the Beadles and Grimm Secret Lair Drop, 
and 2 oil slick treatment cards in the Pharexia COMPLEATED set. Phil Stone was a self taught artist until as of late, 
when he decided to pursue his degree in illustration. Don't let the diploma fool you though, his art is fueled by coffee, 
cigarettes, Pabst Blue Ribbon, and night terrors.

published_fields.bio:
Hugh has been an illustrator in the entertainment industry since 2016. While he got a late start into the industry he has built a client list that includes Wizards of the Coast Magic the Gathering and D&D, Kobold Press, Paizo's Pathfinder, and many independant authors.

Currently he is working as an artist for Magic the Gathering and Dungeons & Dragons. Much of his recent focus has been creating packaging and promotional art for the marketing side of Magic the Gathering. In his personal work he has created a series of images for his Celestialism project.

published_fields.bio: Justine Jones is a self taught artist and illustrator living in Philadelphia, known for her detailed linework and psychedelic colors.  She's done many cards for Magic the Gathering including the Kaleidoscope Killers Secret Lair, many dnd rulebook cards, and the Selfless Spirit promo.  You may have also seen her work in the Ennie Award winning tabletop adventure, Halls of the Blood King.  Justine's work is heavily inspired by the comic books and video games that she grew up with, as well as fairy tales and mythology.

Kai Carpenter's paintings celebrate lush fantasy worlds and the wondrous beings who populate them. Through immersive design, he strives to impart the sense that you, too, inhabit these parts unknown. Kai's work has appeared in several publications including Spectrum Fantastic Art, Infected by Art, and Juxtapose; he earned the 2021 Chesley award for best color and was honored as a finalist in Beautiful Bizarre's international art prize. Kai's art has appeared on trading cards, tabletop games, comic and book covers and in galleries as well as the national parks.

published_fields.bio:
"Hieu Nguyen, artistically known as kelogsloops, is an Australian artist who delives into introspective themes, exploring dreams, the subconscious and the surreal. Often emotively charged,
his paintings are intended to feel like glimpses into intimate, fleeting moments of his subject matter. His works invite viewers to immerse themselves in the quiet narratives woven into his art, offering a view into an ethereal world.
Influenced by music, film, and video games, Hieu's artistic journey began in childhood, where he often lost himself in sketchbooks, drawing inspiration from manga, video games and media shared by his older brothers. It wasn't until late high school and early adulthood that he began refining his craft with greater intention, studying the works of masters such as Monet, Gustav Klimt, and Alphonse Mucha, alongside contemporary artists like Lois van Baarle, Yoshitaka Amano, Agnes Cecile, Anna Dittman, and James Jean.
Over time, Hieu developed a signature style that blends traditional and digital techniques, weaving dimensionality throughout his compositions. These works are often characterised by gilded gold leaf accents, flat graphic elements, stark negative space, expressive watercolour abstractions, and delicately rendered figures in soft realism. His paintings have been exhibited in both group and solo shows worldwide, with frequent showcases in Los Angeles, New York, and Melbourne. In recent years, his work has also entered the realm of Wizards of the Coast's Magic: The Gathering, contributing several artworks to the iconic franchise.
Beyond his own artistic practice, Hieu is a passionate advocate for art education. Since the early stages of his career, he has shared his creative journey transparently, offering in-depth process insights across his social media platforms, which have garnered a following of over two million. His commitment to education has expanded into global watercolour workshops, where he aims to challenge the perception of watercolour as merely a hobbyist's medium. Through his teaching, he hopes to inspire both art enthusiasts and professionals alike, fostering a deeper appreciation for the medium. His artistic philosophy is embodied in his personal motto: 'be right back, chasing dreams.'"

Slovakian illustrator Martina FaÄkovÃ¡ finished her masters degree in Psychology and immediately turned her sights on the world of art. Bringing to bear her keen interest in the human experience and a hunger to constantly improve, she's been working towards sharing a point of view based in striking, dramatic darkness, and in the absolute visual reality of the world around us. Two years later, her work has been awarded and featured in Beautiful Bizarre Magazine, ImagineFX, Forbes Slovakia, and in Spectrum: The Best in Contemporary Fantastic Art. Selected clients include Wizards of The Coast, Tor Books, Orbit Books, Blizzard Entertainment, HarperCollins Publishers, CD Project Red.

Nino Vecia is a freelance illustrator working for companies like Wizards Of The Coast (Magic the Gathering and Dungeons and Dragons), Blizzard, and Marvel just to name a few. Obsessed with dark fantasy art, Nino aims to create works that are both haunting and beautiful.

Lena is a fantasy illustrator with over 15 years of career behind her belt and extensive background in world building, costume making and calligraphy. She had been Magic The Gathering illustrator since 2018

Born in 1996, Ben did not start pursuing art seriously until he was eighteen. Without any sort of local schools or classes, he chose to be a self-taught digital and traditional artist. Over the last 6 years Ben spent most of his focus taking mentorships under artists such as Scott M Fischer, Winona Nelson, David Palumbo and Cynthia Sheppard with a focus on Magic: The Gathering Art In his work. His work has been published in Spectrum and Infected By Art. He has a love for experimenting with movement, texture, and pattern and tries to learn something new with every piece.

published_fields.bio:
Since his first illustrations for Magic's Ice Age (1995), Randy is celebrating crossing the 200th illustration line, his latest art being found in Wilds of Eldraine. Working with traditional media (outside of Universes Beyond, of course), his richly colored artwork has appeared recently on the following, among others: Urza's Incubator (DOM), Sol Ring (Elvish) (LTC),  Fierce Guardianship (CMM), and Sword of Hearth and Home (MH2).
He lives and works in Santa Rosa, CA

Richard Kane Ferguson is an internationally renowned fantasy artist, comic artist and illustrator who has worked extensively in the gaming industry since the 1990s. He's been painting and designing for MTG almost since its beginning, working on its earliest sets right up to the present day. He's lent his distinctive visual style to a host of iconic cards from Dakkon Blackblade to Force of Will. And he's probably at his creative happiest when chained to his drawing board and cranking on a really tight MTG deadline.
RKF has worked with many other gaming and comic companies, including White Wolf Games and Marvel Comics. He's published numerous comics of his own creation. 
RKF is also currently working on the completion of his creator owned opus The Golden Age: The Book of Xell. This lavish, fully painted work first saw print as a 50-page graphic novel in Heavy Metal Magazine. It's designed, written and painted by Richard and will be collected as a stand-alone Graphic Novel, The Lost Book of Kings, as soon as the project is completed”with a potential release date in 2024.
RKF's paintings explore the symbiotic relationships between Man, the natural world and the perceived inner life of his subjects. Through the private lens of the artist, shape, form and spatial relationships are rearranged into his distinctive style of symbolism. He is fascinated by the reoccurring mythic structures inherent within popular culture and how those structures constantly repeat themselves, and pass themselves off as new.

A farmboy from Illinois with a gift for sketching, rk post was planning on a career as a veterinarian until illustration finally took over in his extensive college experience. By his graduation from Northern Illinois University in 1994, rk post was freelancing for the fantasy gaming industry doing interior illustration for several major game companies, gradually teaching himself how to paint with acrylics and eventually oils. rk garnered a staff illustration position at TSR and after its acquisition, continued in this capacity with new parent company Wizards of the Coast painting cover illustrations for games and novels. Passionate about expanding his skill set, rk moved into 2D and 3D art for videogames in addition to his freelance illustrations for Magic the Gathering and other franchises.

Ryan Pancoast has illustrated over 180 Magic cards during his 16-year career. His oil paintings have appeared on popular commanders such as Jonah, the Unifier, Jetmir, Nexus of Revels, and Isshin, Two Heavens as One, and longtime staples such as Wear//Tear, Unburial Rites and Young Wolf.
Ryan's work has been honored by the Society of Illustrators, Art Renewal Center International Salon, Spectrum: The Best in Contemporary Fantastic Art, and Infected by Art. He won Silver in the Oil/Acrylic/Watercolor category in Infected by Art Vol.7 and Gold in IBA 12. In 2024, he won a Chesley Award for Best Gaming Related Illustration.

Sam Burley is a Seattle-based fantasy artist who's worked on MTG since 2011, contributing concept art for dozens of sets and creating over 150 card illustrations. A love for towering mountains and billowing clouds has led his art to be primarily environment focused, but he is a fan of critters both inside and outside of illustration, too! His most popular cards include Supreme Verdict, Prismatic Vista, Nezehal, Glorybringer, Ketria Triome, The Ozolith, and many basic lands including the full-art ˜Nyx' cycle from Theros Beyond Death.

While sources allege there are other interesting things about him, these reports cannot be verified as he is highly reclusive and rarely seen in the wild. Please note that Sam is quite skittish, so approach with caution if spotted, and ideally, bring dogs to pet.

World renown fantasy artist STEVE PRESCOTT has been a major workhorse on Magic:The Gathering since 2005. His concept designs on over a dozen unique sets has helped shape the look of many planes, races, factions, creatures, and characters but his most notable work is on the 250-ish individual cards he has illustrated including fan favorites like Shriekmaw, Chainer-Nightmare Adept, Ellywick Tumblestrum, Arcane Flight, Slaughter Games, Mana Vault (2021), and the 2013 SDCC planeswalkers.

Steven Belledin was raised in Pennsylvania and started his career completing highschool art assignments for his older sisters in exchange for enough money to buy more Swedish fish than he probably should have eaten. After high school he fled small town life to hide among the drones of New York City and become an oil painter. Four years later, he stumbled out of the gates of Brooklyn's Pratt Institute into the harsh light of the "real world" and immediately dove head first into the brick wall of illustration. Though it took him a couple years to recover, he finally began plying his trade in 2000 and continues to plod ahead, tickled that he gets paid to do something he loves. Steven currently resides in Ballston Spa, New York, peering out at the world through the slats of the venetian blinds in his studio windows.

Baxa has been a pro illustrator for over 35 years, for high profile clients. His visceral, innovative character designs and story infused illustrations have been featured in books, magazines, collectible card games (MTG), rpgs (D&D)miniatures, video games, special fx make-up, film and more. As of late, he is expanding his personal work and IPs for publishing and exhibition in galleries in Los Angeles, where he is a member of the LA Dark Art Society movement. Baxa is a published author of Get Work as a Fantasy Artist, and Blood Rituals: The Art of Tom Baxa, and is currently writing and painting an illustrated horror novel, Zombie Coven, featured in his Patreon www.patreon.com/BaxaArt. He enjoys exploring dark themes of the human condition, in order to better understand what drives people. His artwork, prints, books, and more can be seen at www.BaxaArt.com.

Tom Wänerstrand is an American illustrator and Print Production professional in the games industry. The son of Swedish immigrants, Tom began his game career by becoming one of the original 25 illustrators for the seminal game Magic: The Gathering in 1993. He then began a 30-year long journey in the production trade for the game's publisher, Wizards of the Coast. Along the way, Tom continued to illustrate over 60 different unique cards for Magic: The Gathering. His most well known works include classics such as Royal Assassin from the original Alpha release, and Blood Moon from MTG: The Dark. An avid snow skier and boater, you can often find Tom in the mountains and waterways of the beautiful Pacific Northwest region of the U.S. where he lives on an island in the Salish Sea with his wife, son and two occasionally-well-behaved dogs.

Tyler Jacobson is an award-winning illustrator of fantasy and science fiction. His extensive body of work includes countless pieces for Magic: The Gathering and Dungeons & Dragons. Additionally, Jacobson's illustrations have appeared in multiple books and magazines with Simon & Schuster, TOR, Entertainment Weekly, Rolling Stone, Men's Journal, Runner's World, Texas Monthly, The Weekly Standard, and Scientific American, among others. He's been the recipient of both the Jack Gaughan award (2010) and the Spectrum Gold award (2012). In partnership with Flesk Publicatons, Tyler recently published his first art book, "The Art of Tyler Jacobson."

Tyler Walpole has been a valued illustrator in the entertainment industry since the year 2000. His clients include Marvel Entertainment, Wizards of the Coast, Warner Bros Animation, Marvel/Lionsgate, DC Comics, Blizzard, Paizo's Pathfinder, IDW, and Dynamite Entertainment, among many others.

Currently he is working as an artist for Magic the Gathering (Ur Dragon, Lovestruck Beast, Grenzo), handling the art chores on the upcoming Critical Role, Whitestone Chronicles: Ripley graphic novel for Dark Horse (ships spring 2024), and designing the Critical Role miniatures line for Wiz Kids.

Victor Adame Minguez is an independent artist who specializes in imaginative realism, he's widely known for his contributions through his personal work but most notably through the art of Magic, the Gathering. At an early age Victor expressed his passion for many forms of art, from woodworking, sculpture and his love of painting - dreaming to one day make a living as a fantasy artist, it was when Victor discovered Magic the Gathering as it instantly struck a chord - through its social engagement with other people but most significantly, the legendary artists behind the game, wishing to one day work alongside them. Now a 10 year illustration veteran, Victor still remains true to his roots, his work continues to inspire and bring notoriety to the art form, worldwide exposure through Magic, the Gathering has made fans eager to follow his career as he delves deeper into more personal work, further attracting the eyes of viewers around the world.

schedules.title: Draw with a Magic Artist: Vincent Proce
schedules.description: Come learn to draw from one of the artists who helps bring Magic to life!  They'll take you through a step-by-step lesson where you will walk away with your very own sketch that you created! This activity is geared to all ages, and no drawing experience is necessary.

published_fields.bio: Born in 1983, Winona grew up in Duluth, MN, and is now based in Pennsylvania. Winona is a member of the Leech Lake Band of Minnesota Ojibwe, and has worked on "Echo" for Marvel Studios, "Last if Us Part II" for Naughty Dog, and children's books and book covers for Tor, Penguin Random House, Scholastic, and others. She was awarded the 2026 Minnesota Book Award for Children's Literature for "All The Stars In The Sky" by Art Coulson for Simon and Schuster.

Wizard of Barge is a Los Angeles based artist creating a whimsical fantasy universe full of wacky goblins and wizards ! Inspired by the worlds of 90's cartoons, punk-rock, and a juvenile sense of humor, his world invites you to have fun and not take life so seriously. Join the cult!!
